newsitem.title: UK: N Sea crudes see firmer levels, good buying.
newsitem.headline: N Sea crudes see firmer levels, good buying.

text.p: North Sea crudes started an upward climb on Monday as buyers emerged prepared to pay firmer prices, traders said.
"The market is not as long as it seems. There are some buyers there who will pay up and the U.S. is looking more interested in more Brent," one North Sea equity holder said.
A cargo of May 9-11 Statfjord traded on Monday at Dated Brent +11 cents and there were unconfirmed reports of a May 6-8 cargo moving at Dated Brent +8 cents.
A major picked up a May 11-13 Oseberg at a strong dated Brent +15 cents.
That was up from a deal on Friday for a May 2-4 loader at Dated Brent +3 cents.

The one Brent cargo (loading May 6-8) in Monday's paper chains was kept by British Petroleum before the five o' clock deadline. The cargo was expected to be sold on but no firm offer was heard, traders said.

"But the market (for Brent) is firmer than last done (May -55 cents). The U.S. is still there. LLS is very strong," a trader who recently sold Brent to the U.S. said. Light Louisiana Sweet (LLS) crude in the U.S. had firmed 15-17 cents from last Friday talk on Monday.
Intermonth spreads on the Brent market narrowed over the day with May/June trading at -19 cents while June/July narrowed a few cents from early deals at -13 cents to a later trade at -11 cents.
CFD's also narrowed slightly with this week talked around June -44/June -40 cents while next weeks April 28-02 traded early at June -38 cents and narrowed to a deal at June -36.
Good Asian demand for West African crudes saw sellers raise offers and, apart from a few prompt cargoes which were under some pressure, levels were firmer, though no trade was reported.
